searchText: does anyone knows if is it possible to count how many times transactions inside a block make a call to a precompile contract? just looking at etherscan, what it is possible is to check for transactions that involve smart contracts, and then inside the solidity code (if it was made public), parse the code and look for the precompile calls hey <@712691649842642997> this might help i implemented code to check if a tx does a uniswap v3 eth/usdc swap here basically parsing the tx from its traces. maybe you can do something similar for pre-compiles Thanks! where is the code? https://github.com/bharath-123/pepc-boost-testing/tree/tx-data-checks-using-tracing in this repo! The only thing I don't like with the idea of checking solidity code is that it depends on its availability. Would it be possible to know if a precompile was called even when there is no code available? i think as long as the pre-compile is executed as a tx you could maybe check its traces i m not super sure i m not really sure how pre-compiles work tbh lol there are certain EVM memory addresses for that. One alternative could be to check if a contract wrote something into those addresses. <@&857649635274915900> AMA with Zahary from Nimbus starts <t:1696950000:R>. Please come join us and bring some interesting questions 🙂 https://github.com/eth-protocol-fellows/cohort-four/issues/435 Starting now! https://meet.ethereum.org/epf-office-hours Recording from today's AMA with <@553610810652622860> is now up! https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G7DLk1ofO6cV0OXleQYKX9xUIXYOjb0W/view?usp=sharing

excerpts.content: does anyone knows if is it possible to count how many times transactions inside a block make a call to a precompile contract?

excerpts.author: dp_specialist
excerpts.content: just looking at etherscan, what it is possible is to check for transactions that involve smart contracts, and then inside the solidity code (if it was made public), parse the code and look for the precompile calls
